utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case IT-03-66-R77, the Prosecutor versus Beqa Beqaj. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Could we have the appearances for the parties, for the sake of the transcript. Could we have the appearances for the Prosecution, first of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. David Akerson on behalf of the Prosecution, with Jason Dominguez. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you. And could we have the appearances for Defence Counsel, please. MR. VAN DER SPOEL: Good afternoon, Your Honour, my name is Tjarda van der Spoel, Defence counsel, accompanied by my legal assistant Mr. Julius von Bone, attorney-at-law from Rotterdam. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Beqaj, can you hear me in a language you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] You can hear me in a language you can understand; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you very well. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'd like to inform you of the fact that the Chamber to whom this case has been assigned -- to whom this case has been assigned is composed of Judge Liu Daqun, who is the Presiding Judge of Chamber I, and the Judge Szenasi is to my left. I am Judge El Mahdi. I would like to inform the parties that I have been informed of what was discussed at the hearing held pursuant -- or at the meeting held pursuant to Rule 65 ter on the 6th of April 2005, and I'm glad to see that the parties have managed to reach an agreement on a number of issues that concern this case. And I would like to say that the current hearing is taking place pursuant to Rule 73 bis of the Rules of Procedure. I would also like to mention the fact that the Chamber has received the Prosecution's pre-trial brief and the Defence's pre-trial brief. The Prosecution filed its brief on the 17th of January 2005, and the Defence filed its brief on the 22nd of February 2005. Having said that, I would like to point out that everyone has to ensure that this case proceeds rapidly possible. This does not mean that we will not be paying a lot of attention to all the issues concerned, but it is necessary for justice to be rendered as rapidly as possible, and it is necessary to do this in a completely serene manner. I would like it to be clear that the Prosecutor accuses Mr. Beqaj -- charges Mr. Beqaj with three counts. The first count is contempt, the second one attempted contempt, and the third count is incitement to contempt of the Tribunal. I would also like something else to be quite clear, and I'm now addressing the Prosecution. At these charges against the accused, what one might call B1 or B2 in the present case, I'd like to draw the Prosecution's attention to the fact that it was said in the pre-trial brief that the accused tried to get B1 and B2 to change their testimony. Given that this is not quite clear in the indictment, I'd like to know whether the charges concern just one victim, namely B1? Is that the case that the Prosecution would like to make? Are these -- the charges, are the charges against the accused charges that involved trying to influence the witnesses B1 and B2?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to make that crystal clear. These charges pertain to both B1 and B2. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I wanted to make sure that everything was quite clear and I believe that Defence counsel fully understands the nature of the charges and that the charges will be leveled against the accused because of the two victims, that is to say because of interfering with the Witness B1 and Witness B2. MR. VAN DER SPOEL: Yes, we do, Your Honour. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. We'll now move on to what was said at the 65 ter meeting held on the 6th of April. The Prosecution intends to call five witnesses, and it was said that the Prosecution would require about ten hours to conduct their examination-in-chief. And as for the cross-examination, the time required is estimated to be about eight hours. That amounts to a total of 18 hours or four and a half days, since one day means that we have about four-hour hearing. I believe that the Prosecution could nevertheless reduce the time it requires to eight hours and proceed in a more concise manner. I would make the suggestion, if it is possible, and that would amount to two full days of hearing, without taking into account the time needed for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would like to respond to that. We actually are going to withdraw two witnesses from our witness list. We would like to have the same amount of time and possibly a little more with witnesses B1 and B2 but still keeping it less than our original estimate. We are no longer going to call Howard Tucker or Barney Kelly. They are duplicative and I don't think add to the hearing. We would like to concentrate more on the two civilian witnesses. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] So in fact your attention is to call only three witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Very well. As far as Witness B1 is concerned, how much time do you think you will need for your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: At least one full trial day and possibly one and a half trial days. He's not yet arrived and we have not yet proofed him. So until we do that, it's hard for us to make an accurate calculation. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Well, this worries me somewhat. When are you expecting him to arrive?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: He is to arrive as we speak, sometime this afternoon. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Very well. That's fine, in that case. Are you wear of the fact that we will not be sitting tomorrow and we'll be resuming on Wednesday?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Very well. I would nevertheless like to ask you to reconsider your position, and I assure you that examination will be conducted under the benevolent gaze of the Trial Chamber and the Trial Chamber believes that you should be in a position to expedite the proceedings. Nevertheless, you do claim that you require ten hours for your examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Are you referring to total examination time? JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] In chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think it could be less than that but I need to stand by our original estimate. JUDGE EL MAHDI: So it's a maximum?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: It's a maximum. Definitely a maximum. We will do everything we can to try and do it in less time. JUDGE EL MAHDI: And as regards the exhibits, it's 14 exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: 14 exhibits, yes, Your Honour. JUDGE EL MAHDI: Thank you. [Interpretation] Very well. Defence counsel, do you believe that you will be needing eight hours to cross-examine the three witnesses? We won't be having five witnesses now, since the Prosecution has withdrawn two witnesses from its list. MR. VAN DER SPOEL: Your Honour, I think that Defence would need about five or six hours at the maximum. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. In order to prepare now for the commencement of the actual trial, and we will start with opening statements. First we will hear the Prosecution's opening statements. I would like to know how much time you believe that you will require for your opening statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: I estimate that it would be less than 15 minutes, about ten minutes, ten to 15 minutes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you. And will Defence counsel also be making an opening statement or would you like to take advantage of your right to make your opening statement after the Prosecution has closed its case? MR. VAN DER SPOEL: Your Honour, the Defence would like to make an opening statement, though it would be short, about -- JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Immediately afterwards? MR. VAN DER SPOEL: Immediately afterwards. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Very well. There is one other issue I would like to draw Defence counsel's attention to. If I have understood this correctly, it is your intention to call the witness -- call the accused to testify as a witness. I would like you to explain to your client the difference between his status as an accused and as an accused he can make a statement, but not under oath, and his status as a witness who testifies under oath. I would like Mr. Beqaj to fully understand the distinction one has to make between these two roles that he can play pursuant to the rules governing this Tribunal. Could you please discuss this matter with Mr. Beqaj to make sure that his position is quite clear with regard to this matter. I'm not asking you to provide me with an immediate response but I would nevertheless like you to discuss the matter with your client as soon as possible and to inform the Trial Chamber of your discussion as soon as possible. MR. VAN DER SPOEL: Your Honour, I would like to react because I have spoken to my client in extenso last Thursday and one of the items of discussion was this item you just mentioned. He will not testify as a witness. He would like to use the provision as meant in Rule 84 bis of the rules on evidence and procedure. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Very well. After your opening statement, is that the time you are referring to? MR. VAN DER SPOEL: That would be perfect, thank you. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Having dealt with those matters, I would also like to refer to a decision that was rendered today by the Trial Chamber, a decision that concerns the Defence motion contesting the legal nature of the order for detention. The decision was rendered by the Chamber this very day. I believe that at this point in time, we should adjourn and we will resume in about half an hour, because this is the time the technicians require in order to change the tapes. Before we adjourn, I would like to ask the Prosecution the following. If I have understood you correctly, the Prosecution will be requesting protective measures for a certain witness. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The witness that will be testifying today, B2, will need face and voice distortion. And there is -- JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Allow me to interrupt you. I apologise, but I believe that this is a request that was made in your principal motion because the Trial Chamber rendered a decision granting protective measures for Witness B1, but as far as Witness B2 is concerned, if I'm not mistaken, correct me if I am, but if I'm not mistaken, you only requested a pseudonym for this witness. Are there any new circumstances that have arisen in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That is quite correct that in our original motion that we only asked for a pseudonym. We are making a new application today for those additional protection measures. Our first chance to interview this witness, the lawyers that is, was yesterday, and several things became clear to us. One is that the information that he was going to be disclosing when he testified was going to identify B1, and that's the real concern and it's also going to identify other members of the family. And he is such a well known member of the community that any recognition of B2, who is a relative of B1, also identifies B1. The protection measures of B1, of course, emanate from the Limaj trial. We had filed an application to continue them in this trial but they started there, and I think frankly it was an oversight, that it should have been included in the first motion because B1 and B2 are so inextricably intertwined that you can't protect one and not protect the other because either one will identify the other. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] But would you like the hearing to be held in private session? Is that what you are requesting? Or are you requesting facial distortion?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: That's the next issue that I'd like to address. The other thing that became apparent to us -- I mean in principle, it would be okay to have the protection measures in place. However, we think it's going to be very difficult for B2, and possibly B1, although that remains to be seen until we meet with him tomorrow, but at least as far as B2 goes, he's an elderly gentleman and we attempted to have him discuss with us this case using the pseudonyms that were proposed and it was very difficult for him, and we don't think that he can abide by those measures when he's testifying, and I think closed session is probably the only way or the most efficient way that we can proceed through the testimony of B2, and possibly of B1 but particularly of B2. I think the alternative is going to be that we are going to be in and out of private session and we are going to be doing an extraordinary amount of redaction. There are several aspects of this case that are highly dangerous. B1 has been in witness protection since late 2003 in an undisclosed country. He's had two assassination attempts on his life. He's had countless direct threats to himself and his family. Any mention of the country that he's living would put him in great jeopardy; any mention of his name puts him in great jeopardy, and there are a number of other aspects like that that identify B1 which is the ultimate concern here, and so I think the safest course of action for us is actually to proceed with B2 in closed session. We can attempt to try to do it in -- JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] I understand that, but you would agree that the public nature of the proceedings is also of considerable importance, and this is something that we should bear in mind. And if we have three witnesses and we go into closed session for two of them, the entire case will remain an enigma.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think -- my response would be I think a practical solution to this problem would be that we can release the transcript of the closed session hearing after it's fully redacted, and I think that allows us to secure what is a highly dangerous situation for Witness B1, and this entire case is about witness interference and about the protection of witnesses so it would be highly ironic that we compromise a witness's safety in a case that is designed to secure a witness. But I think that would be a reasonable compromise that would allow the public to have access to the proceedings, at the same time maximising the security to the witnesses in the case. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes, but as far as this compromise is concerned -- I'll now address Defence counsel and I would like to know whether Defence counsel has any comments to make with regard to this issue. MR. VAN DER SPOEL: Yes, Your Honour, Defence counsel does have comment. I join your concern about having too many closed sessions because there are people in public who want to witness this trial, and my client is also very concerned that his people, his friends, his family, can see what happens on trial, and that is not only a secret trial. Perhaps a suggestion could be that the Court acts like in the Limaj case. I followed part of that case. That when it was very, very necessary, it was private session, and when it wasn't necessary, open session. So that's what I would suggest to your Tribunal, to your court. JUDGE EL MAHDI: But you are speaking about private or closed session in the Limaj? MR. VAN DER SPOEL: In Limaj the B1 was also heard as a witness and part of the hearing was in private -- in closed session and part of it was in open session. And I think that worked quite well. I didn't follow everything in it so that's a suggestion I would like to make to your court. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you. What is the Prosecution's opinion?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Our position remains the same, Your Honour, particularly as it pertains to B2, who is older, and I think less -- I mean, we've spent a day with him and we know that he's less able to use the pseudonyms consistently, without compromising the identity of the witness. It is possible that we go from open to private and then closed where necessary, and I'm happy to try that but it's going to be I think more of an administrative burden. But if that's the desire of the Court, we are happy to try to proceed that way. I would like to point out the exhibits in this case are primarily recorded telephone calls or intercepted telephone calls that are audio files and we plan to play the audio for Your Honours. It's impossible for to us redact the audio, so for every one of those exhibits as it's played that's going to need to be in at least private session because -- JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes, but we could go into private session to hear the audio recordings. I apologise for interrupting you but my question is, if I have understood you correctly, you are suggesting that we start in open session, but that protective measures be granted in the form of face and voice distortion. So you maintain -- you stand by your position that these witnesses should have voice and facial distortion in a hearing held in open session? I'm now referring to Witness B2.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: As it pertains to Witness B2, at all times face afternoon voice distortion have to be maintained, and our position would be that it should be done in closed session and then secondarily in private session. Open session would be our last option. They have to be protected in terms of their face and their voice. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber believes that in order to respect the need to have public trials, and also in order to respect the need to fully protect witnesses, protective measures should be granted, the protective measures requested. A pseudonym will be used, and there will be voice and facial distortion, but this shall take place in open session. However, if it is necessary, we can go in to closed session. Having said that, is the witness present? After you have made your opening statement, will you immediately be calling the witness to testify?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. In that case, we will now adjourn and have half an hour break. We'll resume at 20 past 3.
